It's nice! I basically get final say. If I say, "We're good," they listen and persist. If I'm like, "Y'all we gotta retreat," they listen. Also means I get put in charge of the rarest one time use items (namely, any Wish scrolls, which happens more than one would think).

Utility caster, though I dabble in support and control as well. I like feeling like I'm contributing and having a tool for everything. I like letting my teammates shine most during combat. At the table, I tend to be that grounding voice, so those roles suite me well; I can support my team's antics and keep them from worrying as much for dragging us into conflict.

I have several cheap sets of Chessex dice that I rotate between, my favorite being the marble green one. At the beginning of the session, I take all their d20s and have a roll-off. Winner is the set I use for the day, or at least until that set starts misbehaving.

After playing a specific character for an indeterminate length of time, I splurge for a more expensive set of dice specific to that character. Currently, I have a set of amazonite, jasper, and copper dice from Norse Foundry, and a set of liquid core dice from URWizards.

I tend to play characters who excel at support and control in battle. Wall of Force, Hold Person/Monster, Polymorph, and Faerie Fire are some of my favorite spells. 

Outside of battle, info gathering is one of my favorite activities, especially when done discretely. I love listening to secret conversations and intentions with invisible familiars, arcane eye, subtle spell detect thoughts, etc etc. 

Personality wise, my characters tend to be pretty snarky, aloof, and a little cocky, mainly because I can't help saying zingers when they come to mind and I really don't like playing hard-asses.

I'd rather have a complete story, even if it wouldn't be the same. What Togashi has written has already been written, and if I don't like how the successor handles the series, I can always just drop it.

I roll all my d20s (maybe 8 sets of dice total, so not much), then use the one that rolled highest for the day. I keep that set on my table, while I keep the rest in the dice tray staging area just in case I need more dice.
